name: Ronan Vidal
life: “I still remember the last flag I mended by candlelight.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Ronan by a small Tuesday habit. Ronan starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I sew flag repairs by the piece. All the flags came in at once and I won't have enough for autumn.
appearance: Ronan has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a charcoal zip cardigan with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. In conversation Ronan counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Ronan is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Ronan loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To spread flag repairs far enough to bridge autumn.
family: Martin Arrieta is Ronan’s stepsibling. A relative came back from a stay in hospital to a house rearranged for convenience and walked straight into the new chair. The family learned to ask before making helpful changes. Ronan will change a whole arrangement back without arguing. Asked about *Overdue by a lifetime*, Martin says, “I can tell which classroom it came from by the paste we used in winter.”
connections: Catherine Easton. A traveling summer contract looks different from the viewpoint of the worker who mends its flags.

reactions.response: Ronan asks both workers what commitments they made on the strength of the old end date.
